why_this_span_and_not_the_long_worked_ex.reasoning: SourceStopContract carries ONE span, and that span has to justify all three fields it stamps: anchor, extreme, include_wick. This one does, verbatim - 'the fair value candle' (anchor is the CANDLE, not the gap band), 'the bottom of' (the extreme), 'include the wick of the candle as well' (include_wick=true).
why_this_span_and_not_the_long_worked_ex.the_honest_wrinkle: This is the teacher's RULE STATEMENT, and he speaks it over the SHORT worked example (he says 'click the short tool here' at char ~13320). The LONG worked example at {18758,18852} says 'We would put our stop to the low of the fair value gap would be just there including the wick' - which resolves DIRECTION for the long side but names the GAP, not the candle.
why_this_span_and_not_the_long_worked_ex.why_that_does_not_weaken_the_long_side: AR-1063 and AR-1068 SS2/SS3.1 already adjudicated this: a gap boundary (high[i-2] on the bullish side) is a price level with no wick to include, so 'including the wick' in BOTH phrasings can only refer to the candle. The long side is TEXT_SUFFICIENT per AR-1068 SS3.1 and is not being re-litigated here.
why_this_span_and_not_the_long_worked_ex.what_is_NOT_claimed: That this span resolves the SHORT side. It does not. The very same words say 'bottom' over a short setup, which is incoherent for a short, and that is exactly why the short side stays refused.
